text:
Maya: Latewatch handoff from me. Quick snapshot — two things I’m actively watching and actions taken below.

Maya: Incident A — regen latency spike in eu-west1 around 23:22 UTC. 95th p50->p95 jumped to ~320ms for >512-token requests. Mitigation: scaled dedicated pool + bumped regen HPA min replicas to 4. Applied temporary request-level rate limit to /v1/regen (50r/s) while we triage.

Maya: Incident B — embed-ingest queue backpressure; ingress lag ~4–6m due to a burst of customer batch uploads. Mitigation: enabled backpressure bypass for high-priority orgs and increased worker concurrency for embed-processor.

Maya: What I did earlier: rolled back PR #4428 (bad quantization knobs), restarted 2 regen pods, verified KV cache warmup on new pods. Ran quick smoke on staging (small prompt) — ok.

Maya: Blockers / asks: 1) Need SRE to confirm whether autoscaler logs show any pod OOMs for regen in the last 2 hours. 2) @Jordan can you check the model-quant rollout logs — regressions alert traces point at quantize-step.

Jordan: Got it. pulling the quant rollout logs now — will link traces here in a minute. Also checking HPA events for regen.

Sasha: I can take the night shift. If latency climbs after 00:30 UTC, I'll flip the fallback-policy to model-variant-stable (low-quant) and open the bridge. :thumbsup:

Liam: Noted on the HPA change. If you need a quick diag, run:
```
kubectl -n prod get hpa regen-deploy -o yaml | egrep -A3 "metrics|conditions"
```
I'll watch for OOMs and post if anything shows.

Priya: For embed-ingest: queued batches > 10k items are the culprit. I queued a manual reprocess for one failing org to reduce backlog. Can we keep the bypass on for 2 hours?

Maya: Yes, keep bypass for 2h. Notify if backlog doesn't drop below 1m.

deploy-bot: Deploy 2024-11-06T23:10Z completed for release/regen-fix. Tags: release/regen-fix@sha256:abcd1234 :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-827 (regen-latency-eu-west1). Severity: S2. Slack bridge: <#incident-827>

Jordan: Quick trace link: https://trace.prod/redwood/trace/8a7f2a — shows heavy CPU spikes during quantize kernel selection. Also saw one pod restart at 23:15 UTC (node g4dn-9).

Sasha: I'll plan to scale down model size for canary traffic after 00:15 if spikes recur. Leaving a canary window open for 30m.

Liam: FYI I don't see OOMs, but kernel panics correlate with a specific driver update on node g4dn-9 — nodes in that pool show the same driver version. Opening an infra ticket to roll node image back if we see more restarts.

Priya: Backlog trending: 1.1m -> 650k over last 25m after worker concurrency bump. Good signal but still noisy.

Maya: Next steps for night:
- Sasha takes lead on regen fallback and canary adjustments.
- Jordan to continue quant rollout log triage & post any relevant traces.
- Liam to watch node pool and infra ticket.
- Priya to keep embed backlog under 500k; escalate if it flattens.

Maya: If anything new pops up ping @channel and add to the incident thread. I'm available for the first 30m of the handoff. Thanks all. :v:
